theory.intro: A **progressive** income tax table splits taxable income into brackets. Each rate applies only to the income above the previous bracket's upper limit. Find the bracket, then the excess, then the tax. Use the table supplied in each question: the Australian table here is the historical $2022$–$23$ table, and other questions use fictional countries.
facts: $\text{Excess}=\text{Taxable income}-\text{Upper limit of the previous bracket}$
A rate written as '$19$ cents for each $\$1$' is $0.19$ as a decimal, and '$32.5$ cents for each $\$1$' is $0.325$.
In the supplied historical Australian table, the first bracket is taxed at nil, so a taxable income of $\$18\,200$ or less has $\$0$ income tax payable.
A bracket's **base tax** is the total tax payable on all the income in the brackets below it.

With these supplied tables, considering income tax only, moving into a higher bracket still leaves some of the extra income after tax. The higher rate applies only to the extra dollars above that boundary.

workedExamples.question_text:
Use these supplied historical $2022$–$23$ tax rules: income up to $\$18\,200$ is taxed at nil; $\$18\,201$ to $\$45\,000$ is taxed at $19$ cents for each dollar over $\$18\,200$; $\$45\,001$ to $\$120\,000$ has base tax $\$5092$ plus $32.5$ cents for each dollar over $\$45\,000$.
Find the bracket and tax payable for (a) $\$17\,400$, (b) $\$35\,600$ and (c) $\$72\,000$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) First bracket: tax $=\$0$.
(b) Second bracket.
Excess $=35\,600-18\,200$.
Excess $=\$17\,400$.
Tax $=0.19\times17\,400$.
Tax $=\$3306$.
(c) Third bracket.
Excess $=72\,000-45\,000$.
Excess $=\$27\,000$.
Tax $=5092+0.325\times27\,000$.
Tax $=\$13\,867$.
The base tax already includes the tax on earlier brackets.

workedExamples.question_text: Use these supplied historical tax rows: $\$120\,001$–$\$180\,000$: base tax $\$29\,467$ plus $37$ cents per dollar over $\$120\,000$; above $\$180\,000$: base tax $\$51\,667$ plus $45$ cents per dollar over $\$180\,000$. Find tax payable on (a) exactly $\$180\,000$ and (b) $\$204\,000$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $\$180\,000$ is the upper boundary of the fourth bracket, so use that row.
Excess $=180\,000-120\,000$.
Excess $=\$60\,000$.
Tax $=29\,467+0.37\times60\,000$.
Tax $=\$51\,667$.
(b) Fifth bracket.
Excess $=204\,000-180\,000$.
Excess $=\$24\,000$.
Tax $=51\,667+0.45\times24\,000$.
Tax $=\$62\,467$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A worker's taxable income increases from $\$116\,000$ to $\$124\,000$. She says that moving into the fourth bracket means all her income will be taxed at $37$ cents per dollar and she will have less money after tax.
Use these supplied historical tax rows: $\$45\,001$–$\$120\,000$: base tax $\$5092$ plus $32.5$ cents per dollar over $\$45\,000$; $\$120\,001$–$\$180\,000$: base tax $\$29\,467$ plus $37$ cents per dollar over $\$120\,000$.
Calculate the tax payable and after-tax income before and after the rise. Explain why she is incorrect.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Before the rise, the taxable income is in the third bracket.
Excess $=116\,000-45\,000$.
Excess $=\$71\,000$.
Tax before $=5092+0.325\times71\,000$.
Tax before $=\$28\,167$.
After-tax income before $=116\,000-28\,167$.
After-tax income before $=\$87\,833$.
After the rise, the taxable income is in the fourth bracket.
Excess $=124\,000-120\,000$.
Excess $=\$4000$.
Tax after $=29\,467+0.37\times4000$.
Tax after $=\$30\,947$.
After-tax income after $=124\,000-30\,947$.
After-tax income after $=\$93\,053$.
Increase in after-tax income $=93\,053-87\,833$.
Increase in after-tax income $=\$5220$.
Only the income above $\$120\,000$ is taxed at $37$ cents per dollar, so she has more money after tax.

workedExamples.question_text:
An employee earns $\$6400$ per month and has no deductions. Use this supplied historical tax row: taxable income from $\$45\,001$ to $\$120\,000$ has base tax $\$5092$ plus $32.5$ cents per dollar over $\$45\,000$.
Calculate the annual income tax payable, to the nearest cent.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Annual taxable income $=6400\times12$.
Annual taxable income $=\$76\,800$.
This is in the third bracket.
Excess $=76\,800-45\,000$.
Excess $=\$31\,800$.
Tax payable $=5092+0.325\times31\,800$.
Tax payable $=\$15\,427.00$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A fictional country has these supplied tax rules: income up to $\$18\,000$: nil; $\$18\,001$–$\$48\,000$: $20$ cents per dollar over $\$18\,000$; above $\$48\,000$: base tax $\$a$ plus $y$ cents per dollar over $\$48\,000$.
(a) Find $a$, the total tax at the previous bracket's upper boundary.
(b) A taxable income of $\$62\,000$ has tax $\$10\,900$. Find $y$.

A fictional country has these supplied annual income tax rules:
Income up to $\$16\,000$: nil.
$\$16\,001$–$\$46\,000$: $20$ cents per dollar over $\$16\,000$.
$\$46\,001$–$\$106\,000$: base tax $\$a$ plus $30$ cents per dollar over $\$46\,000$.
Above $\$106\,000$: base tax $\$b$ plus $40$ cents per dollar over $\$106\,000$.
A bracket's base tax is the total tax payable on all income in the previous brackets. Find (a) $a$ and (b) $b$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The base tax is the tax payable at $\$46\,000$.
$\begin{align*}a&=0.20\times(46\,000-16\,000)\\a&=0.20\times30\,000\\a&=\$6000\end{align*}$
(b) The base tax includes the earlier $\$6000$ and the tax on income from $\$46\,000$ to $\$106\,000$.
$\begin{align*}b&=6000+0.30\times(106\,000-46\,000)\\b&=6000+0.30\times60\,000\\b&=\$24\,000\end{align*}$

Use the tax table to state which tax bracket her taxable income falls into (first, second, third, fourth or fifth).
foundation.solution_text:
$\$79\,400$ is more than $\$45\,000$ and not more than $\$120\,000$.
It lies in the third bracket.

$=0.30\times45\,000$
$=\$13\,500$

$b=13\,500+0.38\times(150\,000-70\,000)$
$=13\,500+0.38\times80\,000$
$=\$43\,900$

mastery.question_text:
A teacher says: "If my taxable income goes from $\$119\,000$ to $\$121\,000$ I move into the $37$c bracket, so all of my income is taxed at $37$c and I end up worse off."
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Use the tax table to find the income tax payable at each taxable income, and explain her error.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Tax on }\$119\,000=5092+0.325\times74\,000$
$=\$29\,142.00$
$\text{Tax on }\$121\,000=29\,467+0.37\times1000$
$=\$29\,837.00$
$\text{Extra tax}=29\,837-29\,142$
$=\$695.00$
The $37$c rate applies only to the $\$1000$ above $\$120\,000$, not to the whole income, so the extra $\$2000$ of income costs only $\$695$ in tax and she keeps $\$1305$ of it.
